title: How this site answers as Himanshu
intro: A static React SPA with a twist: the AI chat is a digital twin that runs entirely in the visitor's browser. This diagram traces the flow from a first click to a deployed build, and why each piece was chosen.

nodes.label: User
nodes.subtitle: browser · any device
nodes.role: The person exploring the site. Every interaction starts here: visiting the page, opening a project, asking the twin a question.
nodes.why: A plain web app keeps the barrier to zero: nothing to install, works on any device. Engineering time goes into the product, not a client.
nodes.tradeoffs: Browsers can't do everything: offline-first apps and deep background work are harder, but for a portfolio the reach wins.

nodes.label: React SPA
nodes.subtitle: React 18 · Vite · strict TS
nodes.role: The single-page app. Every section (about, skills, projects, mission, achievements, blog, contact) renders client-side from shared data files in src/data, so the hero, résumé, terminal, and twin all read the same source of truth.
nodes.why: React with strict TypeScript (tsc -b runs before every build) keeps a growing tree of sections, modals, and easter eggs refactorable. Vite makes dev instant and the production bundle lean.
nodes.tradeoffs: No server-side rendering means first paint waits on JS and search engines see less, a real cost mitigated by a one-page design where the content is the pitch.

nodes.label: Digital Twin engine
nodes.subtitle: phrase-aware retrieval · no-fabrication
nodes.role: The AI chat widget that floats over the site. It scores a question against every knowledge section, picks the best match, fills live facts from the profile and projects, and composes a reply in my voice, entirely in the browser, with no API key by default.
nodes.why: Answers had to be truthful and editable without touching code. Retrieval is phrase-aware: every word of a keyword phrase must appear in the question to score, which separates 'why I want an internship' from 'have I had internship experience' without hardcoded rules. Honesty is an architectural property, not a prompt.
nodes.tradeoffs: Zero-key and fully offline, but the twin can only say what the knowledge files contain: it can't improvise or learn anything new after a deploy. That is the point: it structurally cannot fabricate.

nodes.label: Knowledge files
nodes.subtitle: 7 markdown files · ?raw import
nodes.role: Seven markdown files (personal, education, projects, skills, goals, mission, faq) are imported at build time as raw text via Vite's ?raw transform, then parsed into sections. Each heading becomes a retrievable knowledge unit; a keywords line (or the heading itself) is what the retriever matches against.
nodes.why: Editing the twin is editing a file: add a section or tweak the keywords line and the next build picks it up. No database, no CMS, no migration, and because the files live in git, every fact has a reviewable diff.
nodes.tradeoffs: No content-editor UI, and the twin's knowledge is frozen at build time: answers update on deploy, not live. For a one-person site that trade (truthfulness and versioning over freshness) is the right one.

nodes.label: Remote LLM
nodes.subtitle: VITE_AI_ENDPOINT · optional
nodes.role: When configured, the twin delegates open-ended answers to a real model. The site ships and works without it.
nodes.why: The remote path reuses the same knowledge files as its system prompt, so upgrading answer quality is a config change: the content stays the source of truth.
nodes.tradeoffs: Costs money per request and needs an API key in the build, so it is an opt-in upgrade. If the call fails, the twin silently falls back to the local retriever.

nodes.label: Static build
nodes.subtitle: tsc -b && vite build
nodes.role: npm run build runs the typecheck first (tsc -b), then vite build, emitting a static bundle: HTML, JS, CSS, with the knowledge files embedded inside it. Any CDN or static host can serve it; the twin runs entirely in the visitor's browser.
nodes.why: No server to keep warm and no database to back up: hosting costs almost nothing and can move between GitHub Pages, Netlify, or any CDN by changing one setting. Running the typecheck before bundling means a type error stops a bad deploy before it ships.
nodes.tradeoffs: Nothing computes at the edge: dynamic behavior (the twin, palette, easter eggs) must run client-side, and every deploy rebuilds the whole site. Acceptable because the content is static by design.
